## What the implementation does

- Verifies both fixed parent paths + `contract_sha256` bindings before output, applies REC01–REC26 to a deep copy, proves parent bytes unchanged, reconciles the effective catalogue against the child summaries.
- Emits exactly six phases (roles/schema/types/relations/constraints/indexes/RLS/helper; 9 entry points; 13 trigger functions; 13 trigger declarations; revokes+grants; comments).
- Reconciles 22 declared/21 observed instruction opcodes (`DERIVE_BINDING` absent) and 34/34 expression opcodes; lowers all 22 programs (742 nodes / 14,418 expressions) exactly once; maps every `EXACTLY_ONE` failure to `F_CARDINALITY`/`CF004`; derives one enforcing constraint per all 21 `INSERT_OR_RELOAD_COMPARE` nodes, catches only SQLSTATE 23505, inspects `CONSTRAINT_NAME`, rethrows non-matches, reloads by key+`winner_predicate`, never uses `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`/`WHEN OTHERS`; erases only the canonical constant-false retry marker.
- Independent recognizer tokenizes emitted bytes separately and rejects extra/missing/swapped statements, malformed quotes/dollar bodies, unqualified identifiers, search-path widening, `SECURITY INVOKER`, missing revokes, added trigger grants, application DML, top-level DML/transaction control, psql meta-commands, extension/file/network ops, helper/overload, wrong SQLSTATE/constraint, and output-path escape.

- The `.sql.inert` artifact proves conformance to the renderer's closed static PostgreSQL-16 subset only; it is explicitly **not** a server-parse/catalogue-equivalence claim (a later separately bounded PostgreSQL gate).
